title: Calgary man who threatened to kill Prime Minister Mark Carney in TikTok, YouTube videos pleads guilty
summary: A Calgary man who threatened to kill Prime Minister Mark Carney and one of his children in videos posted to social media pleaded guilty to a number of offences on Friday.

image.caption: Jamie Dacosta, left, pleaded guilty to threatening to kill Prime Minister Mark Carney. (YouTube, Jon Blacker/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Calgary·New
A Calgary man who threatened to kill Prime Minister Mark Carney and one of his children in videos posted to social media pleaded guilty to a number of offences on Friday.
Jamie Dacosta, 31, pleaded guilty to extortion, uttering threats, mischief over $5,000
WARNING: This story contains graphic details
“We’re going to slaughter Mark Carney,” said Jamie Dacosta in a YouTube video posted four days before the prime minister was set to visit Red Deer, Alta.
“We’re coming for you and your children.”
Jamie Dacosta, 31, pleaded guilty to extortion, uttering threats and mischief over $5,000.
Details of the crimes come from an agreed statement of facts (ASF) prepared by prosecutor William Tran and defence lawyer Adriano Iovinelli.

items: Calgary man accused of threatening to kill Prime Minister Mark Carney

blocks.text: According to the ASF, police first warned Dacosta in March after he posted a video to TikTok in which he threatened to slit the throat of one of Carney’s children and disfigure the prime minister.
'Slaughter Mark Carney'
Four months later, Dacosta posted another video, this one on his YouTube account, telling followers he was going to Ottawa.
“We are going to slaughter Mark Carney … hey man, I’ll break the rules for us,” he said in the video.
Two days later, on July 27, Dacosta threatened to hang the PM.

“Mark Carney, you know what we are going to do to you? We are going to put 6x6s on an upside-down cross, and we’re going to hang you upside down butt naked and we’re going to watch all the blood pour out of your skull,” Dacosta said.
Arrested day before Alberta visit

Carney was scheduled to visit Red Deer on July 29 for a housing announcement alongside Alberta Premier Danielle Smith and Mayor Cindy Jefferies. That scheduling information was publicly available online, the ASF notes.
Calgary police and RCMP officers arrested Dacosta at his northeast home on July 28. During an interview with police after his arrest, Dacosta admitted to making the videos.
Friday’s plea also encompassed a six-month period of near-constant harassment Dacosta committed against employees of Tiremaxx, a local tire shop.

In October 2025, Dacosta bought a set of tires from the shop. After the tires were installed, he witnessed a routine test drive and became enraged, demanding $400 for what he believed to be damages caused during the drive.
6 months of harassment

When the company denied the damages and refused to pay, Dacosta spent the next six months threatening, extorting and posting racist comments to his YouTube channel against Tiremaxx owners and employees.
In July, Dacosta showed up at Tiremaxx with an axe and smashed its windows.
By then, he was demanding $10,000 from the company.
A pre-sentence report was ordered ahead of a sentencing hearing which will take place before Justice Clarissa Pearce next year.
